A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RLEdit research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–G. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments, efficiency measurements, capability evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2, 4, and 5 and Figures 3–8.

M1.justification: The hypernetwork, reward components, trajectory-level training, and editing procedures in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix F's proposed extensions are future work, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ZsRE, FEVER, and CounterFact editing tasks and six downstream capability tests. Newly discussed knowledge graphs and multi-hop extensions are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables and figures, including the retrained MEND/MALMEN variants and their RLEdit integrations. The newly cited AnyEdit is discussed only as a future direction.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same models, dataset preparation, metrics, editing configurations, and timing procedures. Table 3's hyperparameter values are unchanged despite formatting revisions.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same component ablations, sequence-length evaluations, capability tests, and batch-size/edit-frequency analysis. Appendix G's dataset examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting in Tables 2 and 5 is identical. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and reported trends are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 5 replaces one missing-result hyphen with an en dash; this does not change a result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward equations, MDP formulation, and Appendix E proof are retained without substantive revision. Minor mathematical typesetting differences do not alter their meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, effectiveness, efficiency, and lifelong-editing claims, including the headline 59.24% improvement and 2.11% time figures.

C2.justification: Appendix F connects the retained layer-selection observation to interpretability-guided editing and adds proposed extensions to other editing paradigms and knowledge graphs for multi-hop knowledge. It also expands discussion of hallucination and security research, while Section 5's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hardware, precision, preprocessing, hyperparameters, pseudocode, and the code-access statement are unchanged. The added future-work discussion supplies no new reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Eight references are added to support Appendix F's discussion of interpretability, broader editing methods, knowledge graphs, hallucinations, and safety. This is a limited contextual expansion; the main related-work account and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix F receives a local paragraph revision and additional future-work prose. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while the main narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains heavier outer rules and more spacing between dataset groups, and Table 5 standardizes one missing-result dash. Added references and discussion cause local text reflow; all figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds contextual references and future directions in Appendix F, alongside modest table-formatting refinements. These additions remain prospective and do not resolve the already acknowledged multi-hop limitation or change the explanations and evidence supporting the central claims. The overall scientific and reporting quality remains materially the same.
